title: Root perturbation in a complete one-dimensional local domain
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means that $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal and domain means nonzero with no zero divisors. Assume $\dim R=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and that $R$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Fix $0\ne t\in\mathfrak m$, a polynomial $P\in R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and $a\in R$ with $P(a)=0$ and $P^{\prime}(a)\ne0$, where $P^{\prime}$ is the formal derivative. For every integer $c\ge0$ there exists an integer $n\ge1$ such that, for every polynomial $Q\in R[T]$ all of whose coefficients belong to $t^nR$, there is $b\in R$ satisfying $(P+Q)(b)=0$ and $b-a\in t^cR$. No invertibility of $P^{\prime}(a)$ in $R$, monicity of $P$, or bound on the degree of $Q$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09EI, lemma-krasner, proof with the chosen nonzero parameter t: the constructed root differs by an element of (t^c). This is the principal-parameter precision form of the displayed maximal-ideal precision statement; Noetherianity is made explicit.

proof.text: Put $d=P^{\prime}(a)\ne0$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. By [lem-sc-local-domain-dim-one-principal-localization-fraction-field], applied with $B=R$ and $f=t$, the canonical map $R[1/t]\to K$ is an isomorphism: the local-domain, dimension-one and nonzero maximal-ideal-element hypotheses are exactly those of the item. By [def-weil-ring-localization-away], the inverse image of $d^{-1}$ is $u/t^M$ for some $u\in R$ and $M\ge0$. Thus $du=t^M$ in $R$, since a domain injects into its fraction field. Choose $C=\max\{c,M+1\}$ and $n=M+C\ge1$. These choices depend only on $P,a,t,c$, not on $Q$.

source.place: Tag 09EI, lemma-krasner, proof: denominator bound, Taylor expansion, Newton induction and passage to the limit; indices start at C rather than the denominator exponent.

proof.text: Fix any allowed $Q$ and write $F=P+Q$. The finite-sum definition of a polynomial [def-weil-polynomial-ring] gives the identities $P(x+h)=P(x)+P^{\prime}(x)h+h^2A(x,h)$ and $P^{\prime}(x)-P^{\prime}(a)=(x-a)B(x,a)$ for polynomials $A,B$ over $R$: expand each monomial by the binomial formula, putting the terms of degree at least two in $h$ into $h^2A$, and use $x^i-a^i=(x-a)\sum_{j=0}^{i-1}x^{i-1-j}a^j$ for the second identity. The same difference identity for each monomial of $Q$ gives $Q(x+h)-Q(x)\in t^nhR$. Also $Q(x)\in t^nR$. These are finite sums for every $Q$, with no uniform degree bound needed.

source.place: Tag 09EI, lemma-krasner, proof: denominator bound, Taylor expansion, Newton induction and passage to the limit; indices start at C rather than the denominator exponent.

proof.text: Construct $x_k$ for integers $k\ge C$ with $x_k-a\in t^CR$, $F(x_k)\in t^{M+k}R$ and $x_{k+1}-x_k\in t^kR$. Set $x_C=a$; then $F(a)=Q(a)\in t^{M+C}R$, so the base case holds. Given $x_k$, let $e_k\in R$ be the unique element with $F(x_k)=t^{M+k}e_k$ (existence is the invariant and uniqueness follows from $t\ne0$ in a domain). Put $\delta_k=-ut^ke_k$ and $x_{k+1}=x_k+\delta_k$. Then $\delta_k\in t^kR\subseteq t^CR$, so the closeness invariant persists, and $F(x_k)+d\delta_k=0$ because $du=t^M$.

source.place: Tag 09EI, lemma-krasner, proof: denominator bound, Taylor expansion, Newton induction and passage to the limit; indices start at C rather than the denominator exponent.

proof.text: The polynomial identities of Step 2 [def-weil-polynomial-ring] now give $F(x_{k+1})=F(x_k)+d\delta_k+(P^{\prime}(x_k)-d)\delta_k+\delta_k^2A(x_k,\delta_k)+Q(x_k+\delta_k)-Q(x_k)$. The first two terms cancel. The remaining three terms lie respectively in $t^{C+k}R$, $t^{2k}R$ and $t^{n+k}R$. Since $C\ge M+1$, $k\ge C$ and $n=M+C\ge M+1$, each lies in $t^{M+k+1}R$. This proves the residual invariant at $k+1$ and completes the induction. Only the fixed nonzero derivative $d$ has been divided by in $K$; no derivative was assumed invertible in $R$.

source.place: Tag 09EI, lemma-krasner, proof: denominator bound, Taylor expansion, Newton induction and passage to the limit; indices start at C rather than the denominator exponent.

proof.text: For $k\ge C$, write $x_k-a=t^cy_k$ with the unique $y_k\in R$. Domain cancellation in $t^c(y_{k+1}-y_k)=\delta_k$ gives $y_{k+1}-y_k\in t^{k-c}R$. For every $r\ge1$, these differences lie in $\mathfrak m^r$ once $k\ge\max\{C,c+r\}$, because $t\in\mathfrak m$. Finite telescoping shows that the classes of $y_k$ in $R/\mathfrak m^r$ are eventually constant. Their eventual values are compatible under all quotient projections. By the defining bijection of $\mathfrak m$-adic completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], this compatible family is the family of residue classes of a unique $y\in R$. Put $b=a+t^cy$. In particular $b-a\in t^cR$, without assuming that a principal ideal is closed.

source.place: Tag 09EI, lemma-krasner, proof: denominator bound, Taylor expansion, Newton induction and passage to the limit; indices start at C rather than the denominator exponent.

proof.text: Fix $r\ge1$ and take $k$ large enough that $y_k\equiv y\pmod{\mathfrak m^r}$ and $M+k\ge r$. Then $b-x_k=t^c(y-y_k)\in\mathfrak m^r$ and $F(x_k)\in t^{M+k}R\subseteq\mathfrak m^r$. The polynomial finite-sum formula [def-weil-polynomial-ring], or the monomial difference formula in Step 2, gives $F(b)-F(x_k)\in\mathfrak m^r$. Hence $F(b)$ belongs to every $\mathfrak m^r$. The separatedness included in [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] says that their intersection is zero. Thus $(P+Q)(b)=0$. The same $n=M+C$ works for every allowed $Q$, proving all the claimed quantifiers.

split_report.summary: Six-step Newton proof of Stacks 09EI, reusing the existing one-dimensional local-domain localization theorem. No new nodes or statement changes.

tool_uses.why: Generic dimension-one local-domain algebra tool: it gives the denominator bound d^{-1}=u/t^M needed by the Stacks 09EI Newton proof. No node of the six-functor unit states this algebraic fact.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q149-6861d4586 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 09EI lemma-krasner (more-algebra.tex l.33747-33810), its statement and full proof, and where 09EJ invokes it. The statement is unchanged; it measures precision in powers of t, which is the Stacks proof with pi=t and Noetherianity made explicit, and the citer lem-sfb-dvr-completion-extension-approximation step 2 uses it with t=pi, c=1. Step 1: the cited lemma lem-sc-local-domain-dim-one-principal-localization-fraction-field (hypotheses all present, sorry-free Lean record) and def-weil-ring-localization-away together give du=t^M. Steps 2-4: the Newton induction has an explicit base case and invariants. The residual terms have exponents C+k, 2k and n+k, each at least M+k+1 because C=max(c,M+1); this repairs the source's indexing glitch (iterates start at the denominator exponent m while the source claims precision pi^c). Step 5: domain cancellation gives the divided iterates y_k, and the inverse-limit bijection of def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring gives b in a+t^cR without assuming the principal ideal is closed. Step 6: separatedness (the intersection of the m^r is zero) gives (P+Q)(b)=0. proof_deps is exactly the union of the step uses. Edge cases tested: c=0, unit derivative, Q=0, and k[[s^2,s^3]] with t=s^2, d=s^3 (no DVR or normality needed). No new nodes. Duplicate search over Krasner and root-perturbation nodes found only monic/henselian/field-containment variants, none of which gives this statement. Accepted tool_use: the dimension-one localization lemma from sk-thm-curveestimate, a generic denominator bound that no node of this unit gives. No changes made.
